precepts.why:
Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord”, and Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” What happened to Cain and Abel physically is a foreshadowing of Jacob and Esau spiritually: one is chosen and one is not.

Paul explains it with Rebecca’s twins: “For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth”. Then: “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Cain was not rejected because he was wroth; that was ordained from the beginning. It is about election, the purpose God makes. He can make one vessel for one use and another vessel of wrath fitted for destruction.

Christians take “not of works” to mean the law need not be kept. What it tells us is that from the foundation God chose his elect. He still requires the works of the law, not the sacrificial law, but being clean and repented, to obtain the kingdom of heaven. When the first world was formed every nation was supposed to follow the laws, and judgment followed whoever did not. Cain’s rebellious nature showed itself, and it continues to this day in Esau.

People say God doesn’t hate, and they isolate “God is love.” But notice it says “as it is written”: it is in the Bible. It was written first in Malachi: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” Edom says, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”, and he did, in the Renaissance. But the Lord says, “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” God lets him rise to power so that he can take him down.

And the Lord asked Cain, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” Remember that, because the same reason Cain hated Abel is the reason Esau hates Jacob today. It is the same spirit; only the name changes. “Satan” simply means adversary, one who obstructs and opposes. That is why everything they do is about us: they were made for that purpose, to obstruct and oppose us, because God purposed it from the beginning.

precepts.why:

The thing made and its maker are both cursed.

Now go to Christ, who is also a maker: he made everything seen and unseen, in earth and in heaven. Paul asks, “Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” It is a rhetorical question, because everything he made is in its perfect form and perfect order. The hummingbirds still go to the nectar, lions still chase the beasts, mothers still give suck to their young, the whales do not get out of the water to walk on land, and the water does not pass the bounds of the sand unless the Lord sends his angels in the storm. Everything is in perfect order except the twelve tribes of Israel. Keep my commandments that you may live, and we said no.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Christ created both. Jacob and Esau came from the same mother and father, the same lump: one a vessel of honour, which we descend from, and the other a vessel of dishonour.

Then: “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. While Esau fulfils his role as God’s sword, the Lord lets him do what he was created for, and what he was created for is destruction. They are here to serve a purpose, and then the Lord is going to destroy them. Wipe your tears: the nations got to go.

So the war of the gods is this: the true Maker whose works stay in order, against the gods men make with hands, which are cursed with the men who made them.

God raised America up. Why? That he might show his power in her. All the technological advances America has, God allowed her to have. There is no nation, no country, that can match Babylon the Great; that is why they call it the great: it has the greatest technology of all nations. Christ says, I must show my power in you, because I am the only one that can take America out.
